name.en: Recorded call: “an arrest warrant has been issued against you”

how.en: Your phone rings, often showing a Luxembourg mobile or official-looking number, and a recording says an arrest warrant has been issued in your name. You are told to press a key or stay on the line to speak to an “officer”, who then asks for personal or bank details, a transfer, or valuables to settle the matter. The number is spoofed. In 2025 the Police reported the recording played in English; in July 2026 they warned of a new wave of these calls.

text.en: A call from what looks like a Luxembourg or official number plays a recording.
The recording says there is an arrest warrant against you.
You are told to press a key or hold for an officer.
The “officer” asks for your details, bank information or a payment.

This is an automated message from the police department. An arrest warrant has been issued under your name for a serious offence. To avoid immediate arrest, press 1 now to speak with the officer in charge of your file.

en: press 1 to speak to an officer
officer asked for my bank details to cancel warrant
call from justice about a warrant
The Police and courts don’t announce arrest warrants with a recorded call.
Being asked to press a key and stay on the line.
Any request for bank details, a transfer or valuables to “settle” a warrant.
A Luxembourg number on screen can be faked (caller ID spoofing).
Hang up at once. Don’t call the number back.
If unsure, contact the Police yourself through the usual channels (113 in an emergency).
If you gave details or paid, call your bank and file a complaint at any police station.

sources.title: Vorsicht vor betrügerischen Telefonanrufen im Namen der Polizei bzw. der Justiz
